'''Raúl Bravo Sanfélix''' (born 14 April 1981) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]] or [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]].

Having played in almost all the youth ranks at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], he went on to have a six-year spell in the first team, where he almost always served as a backup; however, it was during that period that he reached the [[Spain national football team|Spain national side]], representing them at [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]].<ref name=Bravo>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=31243.html|title=Bravo for Madrid youngster|publisher=UEFA|date=28 August 2002|access-date=22 January 2020}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Bravo also spent several years in Greece, most notably with [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] where he won six major titles, including three [[Super League Greece|national championships]].

==Club career==
===Real Madrid===
Bravo was born in [[Gandia]], [[Valencian Community]]. After playing in his early years with two local clubs, he joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s youth system at 16. He was subsequently part of the ''Junior A'' side, and played for them two more seasons before arriving at the [[Real Madrid C|C team]] in [[Tercera División]], moving to [[Real Madrid Castilla]] in [[Segunda División B]] for [[2001–02 Segunda División B|2001–02]].<ref name=Bio>{{cite news|url=https://observador.pt/2019/05/28/a-pobreza-em-gandia-a-champions-em-madrid-a-descida-em-salonica-a-ascensao-e-queda-de-raul-o-antigo-bravo/|title=A pobreza em Gandía, a Champions em Madrid, a descida em Salónica: a ascensão e queda de Raúl, o (antigo) Bravo|trans-title=Poverty in Gandía, the Champions in Madrid, relegation in Thessaloniki: the rise and fall of Raúl, the (former) Brave (pun on his surname)|newspaper=[[Observador]]|first=Bruno|last=Roseiro|language=pt|date=28 May 2019|access-date=31 July 2019}}</ref>

International call-ups of some players in the first team gave Bravo the chance for a [[La Liga]] debut against [[Athletic Bilbao]] at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]], on 6 October 2001, and he played 70 minutes in a 2–0 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2001/10/07/pagina-2/458141/pdf.html|title=Sólo Raúl ya fue bastante|trans-title=With only Raúl it was more than enough|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Nika|last=Cuenca|language=es|date=7 October 2001|access-date=8 June 2018}}</ref> He ended up training with them – under [[Vicente del Bosque]]'s management – very regularly, which eventually led to his permanent stay from the [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03 campaign]] onwards.

In January 2003, Bravo started an unsuccessful six-month loan spell at [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/leeds_united/2714779.stm|title=Leeds sign Real defender|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=31 January 2003|access-date=22 July 2010}}</ref> During [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]], in which he appeared for [[Spain national football team|Spain]], [[Mick McCarthy]], whilst commentating for the [[BBC]], remarked that he looked a different player to the one in his [[Elland Road]] stint; [[Roberto Carlos (footballer)|Roberto Carlos]]' presence, however, restricted his playing time in the Real main squad.<ref name=Bio/>

===Olympiacos===
With a chance to retain [[UEFA Champions League]] status, Bravo signed a four-year contract with [[Olympiacos F.C.]] in mid-July 2007, with the transfer fee estimated in the region of [[Euro|€]]2.3 million while the player received an annual salary of €1.3 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01c3-0ea8c68fc519-cc5e5b59c583-1000--olympiacos-snare-raul-bravo/|title=Olympiacos snare Raúl Bravo|publisher=UEFA|date=12 July 2007|access-date=22 July 2010}}</ref> After having appeared rarely due to injuries, he had a short return to Spain in the 2009 January [[transfer window]], moving on loan to top-tier strugglers [[CD Numancia]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsnetwork.com/merge/tsnform.aspx?c=sportsnetwork&page=soc-spa/news/news.aspx?id=4208102|title=Numancia swoops for trio|publisher=The Sports Network|date=31 January 2009|access-date=23 September 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110525234310/http://www.sportsnetwork.com/merge/tsnform.aspx?c=sportsnetwork&page=soc-spa%2Fnews%2Fnews.aspx%3Fid%3D4208102|archive-date=25 May 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2009/01/31/futbol/equipos/numancia/1233356989.html|title=El Numancia se refuerza con Raúl Bravo, Marian Kelemen y Lago Junior|trans-title=Numancia strengthen with Raúl Bravo, Marian Kelemen and Lago Junior|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=31 January 2009|access-date=23 September 2012}}</ref> and having almost no impact in a [[2008–09 La Liga|relegation-ending campaign]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.desdesoria.es/2013/05/29/breve-enciclopedia-numantina/|title=Breve enciclopedia numantina|trans-title=Brief ''numantina'' encyclopedia|newspaper=Desde Soria|language=es|date=29 May 2013|access-date=16 October 2019}}</ref>

Bravo showed a much higher commitment than in the previous year with Olympiacos and, thanks to his performances in preseason, earned the starting left-back position over [[Didier Domi]] and [[Leonardo Jesus|Leonardo]]. He was released in May 2011 at the age of 30, after having contributed 18 matches to [[2010–11 Super League Greece|the conquest]] of the [[Super League Greece]].

===Later years===
On 31 August 2011, Bravo returned to his country and [[Madrid]], signing for [[Rayo Vallecano]] which had just [[2010–11 Segunda División|promoted to the top division]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/09/01/futbol/equipos/rayo/1314879360.html|title=Raúl Bravo: "Es la situación perfecta para mí"|trans-title=Raúl Bravo: "It's the perfect situation for me"|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=1 September 2011|access-date=1 September 2011}}</ref> In the following off-season, after having been rarely played in his [[2011–12 La Liga|only season]], he joined [[Beerschot A.C.]] in Belgium for one year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.beerschot.be/nl/nieuws/raul-bravo-tekent-bij-beerschot-ac|title=Raul Bravo tekent bij Beerschot AC|trans-title=Raúl Bravo signs at Beerschot AC|publisher=Beerschot AC|first=Ward|last=Callens|language=nl|date=28 August 2012|access-date=28 August 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121231203113/http://www.beerschot.be/nl/nieuws/raul-bravo-tekent-bij-beerschot-ac|archive-date=31 December 2012}}</ref>

Aged 33, Bravo returned to the Greek top flight, moving to [[Veria F.C.|Veria FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kerkidasport.gr/index.php/veria-fc/item/2695-veroia-energopoiithike-i-vomva-me-raoyl-bravo/|title=ΒΕΡΟΙΑ: Ενεργοποιήθηκε η "βομβα" με Ραούλ Μπράβο!|trans-title=Veria: a real "bomb" with Raúl Bravo!|publisher=Kerkida Sport|language=el|date=27 August 2014|access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref> His contract expired on 30 June 2015 and, two months later, he agreed to a one-year deal with [[Aris Thessaloniki F.C.]] also in the country.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.naftemporiki.gr/story/1001933/aris-anakoinose-ton-raoul-mprabo#null|title=Άρης: Ανακοίνωσε τον Ραούλ Μπράβο!|trans-title=Aris: Raúl Bravo announced!|newspaper=[[Naftemporiki]]|language=el|date=11 September 2015|access-date=4 October 2015}}</ref>

==International career==
Bravo was capped for Spain on the [[Spain national under-16 football team|under-16 level]] in 1997–98, when the national team won the ''[[Algarve]] Tournament''. With the [[Spain national under-17 football team|under-17s]] he played in the ''[[Nymburk]] International Tournament'', scoring two goals in three matches.

Bravo's [[Spain national football team|full]] debut was on 21 August 2002 against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]], in a [[Exhibition game|friendly]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/2002/08/22/deportes/1029967201_850215.html|title=Poca luz para tanto estreno|trans-title=Too little light for so many premieres|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Ramón|last=Besa|language=es|date=22 August 2002|access-date=12 November 2015}}</ref><ref name=Bravo/> Subsequently, he was a participant at [[UEFA Euro 2004]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7b44fc5b75-bb339e5a3edf-1000--saez-selects-spain-squad/|title=Sáez selects Spain squad|publisher=UEFA|first=Iván|last=Modia|date=20 May 2004|access-date=22 January 2020}}</ref> playing every minute in Spain's group stage exit campaign, against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]], [[Russia national football team|Russia]] and eventual champions [[Greece national football team|Greece]] (always as a stopper);<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1581/match=1059172/postmatch/report/index.html|title=Greece profit as Charisteas stops Spain surge|publisher=UEFA|first=Matthew|last=Spiro|date=17 June 2004|access-date=7 June 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120619213041/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1581/match=1059172/postmatch/report/index.html|archive-date=19 June 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1581/match=1059180/postmatch/report/index.html|title=Portugal leave Spain in shade to light up Lisbon|publisher=UEFA|first=David|last=Farrelly|date=20 June 2004|access-date=7 June 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005200457/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2004/matches/round=1581/match=1059180/postmatch/report/index.html|archive-date=5 October 2013}}</ref> he was not recalled since, receiving a total of 14 [[Cap (sport)|caps]].

==Controversy==
On 28 May 2019, Bravo was arrested on charges of belonging to a [[Financial crime|criminal organisation]], involved in corruption and [[money laundering]]. The investigation regarded [[match fixing]] during the [[2016–17 La Liga|2016–17]] and [[2017–18 La Liga|2017–18 campaigns]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/05/28/5cecfd24268e3ec9668b45d3.html|title=Spain's match fixing allegations: Who's who of those arrested?|newspaper=Marca|date=28 May 2019|access-date=28 May 2019}}</ref> The following January, he was accused by Serbian tabloid newspaper ''[[List of newspapers in Serbia#Daily newspapers|Telegraf]]'' of hiring a [[Contract killing|contract killer]] to murder his former Olympiacos teammate [[Darko Kovačević]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2020/01/17/5e221d3ee2704ed8308b45d2.html|title=Raul Bravo accused of being behind gun attack on Kovacevic by Serbian media|newspaper=Marca|date=17 January 2020|access-date=24 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2871971-report-raul-bravo-accused-of-hiring-hitman-in-attempt-on-darko-kovacevic|title=Report: Raul Bravo accused of hiring hitman in attempt on Darko Kovacevic|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|first=Gianni|last=Verschueren|date=18 January 2020|access-date=22 January 2020}}</ref> which he vehemently denied, commenting: "It's a crazy story, it's nonsense."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2020/01/20/5e25814b46163f33ac8b45ac.html|title=Raul Bravo: Saying I ordered Kovacevic's death is crazy, it's nonsense|newspaper=Marca|date=20 January 2020|access-date=24 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/658708/real-madrid-raul-bravo-murder-darko-kovacevic/|title='NONSENSE!' Ex-Leeds defender Raul Bravo rubbishes claims he ordered murder of former team-mate Darko Kovacevic|publisher=[[Talksport]]|first=Sean|last=O'Brien|date=21 January 2020|access-date=22 January 2020}}</ref>
